name: Aizoaceae
description: Pigfaces, ice plants and warrigal greens are fleshy-leaved plants that cope with salt and drought.

name: Amaranthaceae
description: Includes beetroot, silverbeet, spinach and many saltbushes.

name: Amaryllidaceae
description: Bulbs and strappy plants, including agapanthus, clivias and the onion family.

name: Anacardiaceae
description: The cashew family, including mangoes and the weedy broad-leaf pepper tree.

toxic.note: The sap of many members can irritate the skin.

name: Apiaceae
description: The carrot family includes carrots, parsley, coriander, dill and fennel. Their flat flower heads feed hoverflies and tiny parasitic wasps.

name: Apocynaceae
description: The dogbane family, including frangipani and star jasmine. Many members have milky sap.

name: Araceae
description: The arum family, including monstera and philodendrons.

toxic.note: The leaves and stems contain calcium oxalate crystals that irritate the mouth and throat.

name: Arecaceae
description: The palms.

name: Asparagaceae
description: A varied family that includes mat-rushes (Lomandra), palm lilies and the weedy asparagus ferns.

name: Asphodelaceae
description: Includes flax-lilies, grass trees and bulbine lilies.

name: Asteraceae
description: The daisy family, the largest family of flowering plants. Its open flower heads offer easy nectar and pollen to many insects.

name: Balsaminaceae
description: Balsams and busy lizzies.

name: Berberidaceae
description: Barberries and nandina.

name: Bignoniaceae
description: Trumpet-flowered vines and trees, including bower and wonga vines and jacarandas.

name: Blechnaceae
description: Hard ferns and rasp ferns.

name: Boraginaceae
description: The borage family, whose blue flowers are favourites of honey bees.

name: Brassicaceae
description: The cabbage family includes broccoli, cabbage, kale, rocket and mustards. Plants left to flower feed bees and hoverflies.

name: Bromeliaceae
description: Bromeliads are rosette plants whose leaf cups hold water.
care_note: Please flush the water out of the leaf cups every week in warm weather, so mosquitoes cannot breed in them.

name: Buxaceae
description: Box and its relatives.

name: Cannabaceae
description: Hemp, hops and hackberries, including the weedy Chinese elm (Celtis sinensis).

name: Caricaceae
description: Papaya (pawpaw) and its relatives.

name: Casuarinaceae
description: She-oaks are wind-pollinated trees whose cones feed black-cockatoos.

name: Commelinaceae
description: Spiderworts, including the weedy wandering trad (Tradescantia).

name: Convolvulaceae
description: The morning glory family, including sweet potato and the weedy blue morning glory.

name: Crassulaceae
description: Succulents such as jade plants, kalanchoes and the weedy mother-of-millions.

name: Cucurbitaceae
description: The gourd family includes pumpkins, zucchini, cucumbers and melons. Most have separate male and female flowers and need bees to set fruit.

name: Cyperaceae
description: Sedges, which grow best in damp ground.

name: Dilleniaceae
description: Includes the guinea flowers (Hibbertia), whose flowers have no nectar and release pollen when buzzed by bees.

name: Doryanthaceae
description: The Gymea and spear lilies of eastern Australia.

name: Elaeocarpaceae
description: Includes blueberry ash and quandongs.

name: Ericaceae
description: The heath family, including blueberries, azaleas and many Australian heaths. Most need acidic soil.

name: Euphorbiaceae
description: The spurge family. Many members have milky sap.

toxic.note: The milky sap of many spurges irritates skin and eyes.

name: Fabaceae
description: The pea and wattle family. Most fix nitrogen in their roots, which enriches the soil.
fertiliser_note: Legumes make their own nitrogen, so they need little or no fertiliser.

name: Geraniaceae
description: Geraniums and pelargoniums.

name: Goodeniaceae
description: Fan-flowers and goodenias, with flowers shaped like a hand or a fan.

name: Haemodoraceae
description: Kangaroo paws and their relatives.

name: Hydrangeaceae
description: Hydrangeas and their relatives.

name: Iridaceae
description: The iris family, including wild irises (Dietes) and gladioli.

name: Juncaceae
description: Rushes, plants of wet ground and pond edges.

name: Lamiaceae
description: The mint family is made up of aromatic herbs and shrubs, such as lavender, salvias, rosemary, basil and coastal rosemary. Their flowers are favourites of bees.

name: Lauraceae
description: The laurel family, including avocados, bay trees and the weedy camphor laurel.

name: Malvaceae
description: The hibiscus family, which also includes flame trees and kurrajongs.

name: Melastomataceae
description: A mostly tropical family whose flowers are often buzz-pollinated.

name: Moraceae
description: The fig and mulberry family.

name: Musaceae
description: Bananas.

name: Myrtaceae
description: The myrtle family includes eucalypts, bottlebrushes, paperbarks, tea trees and lilly pillies. Their flowers are rich in nectar and pollen.

name: Nyctaginaceae
description: Includes bougainvillea, whose colourful bracts surround small flowers.

name: Ochnaceae
description: Includes the weedy Mickey Mouse plant (Ochna).

name: Oleaceae
description: The olive family, including jasmines, privets and olives.

name: Oxalidaceae
description: Wood sorrels, several of which are garden weeds.

name: Passifloraceae
description: Passionfruit and other passion flowers.

name: Pittosporaceae
description: Pittosporums and the native frangipani.

name: Plantaginaceae
description: Plantains and their relatives.

name: Poaceae
description: The grasses. Most are wind-pollinated, so they offer bees little nectar, though some bees collect their pollen.

name: Portulacaceae
description: Portulaca and purslane.

name: Proteaceae
description: A mainly southern family of shrubs and trees, including grevilleas, banksias, hakeas and macadamias. Most are adapted to poor soils.
fertiliser_note: Phosphorus harms most Proteaceae. Please feed only with a native fertiliser labelled low in phosphorus, if at all.

compost.note: A thin layer of leaf mulch suits them better than rich compost.

name: Rosaceae
description: The rose family, which includes apples, pears, strawberries, stone fruit and berries.

name: Rubiaceae
description: The coffee family, including gardenias.

name: Rutaceae
description: The citrus family, which also includes correas, waxflowers and murraya. Many have aromatic leaves dotted with oil glands.

name: Sapindaceae
description: The soapberry family, including hop bushes, lychees and the weedy balloon vine.

name: Scrophulariaceae
description: Includes emu bushes (Eremophila) and boobiallas (Myoporum).

name: Solanaceae
description: The nightshade family includes tomatoes, capsicums, eggplants and potatoes, as well as petunias and wild tobacco.

toxic.note: The leaves, stems and green fruit of many nightshades contain toxic alkaloids such as solanine.

name: Strelitziaceae
description: Bird of paradise plants.

name: Theaceae
description: The tea family, including camellias.

name: Tropaeolaceae
description: Nasturtiums.

name: Verbenaceae
description: The verbena family, which includes lantana and golden dewdrop.

name: Violaceae
description: Violets and pansies.

name: Zingiberaceae
description: The ginger family.

name: Acanthaceae
description: Bear's breeches, thunbergias, justicias and polka dot plants are mostly tropical herbs, shrubs and twining vines with tubular, often two-lipped flowers and colourful bracts.

name: Aquifoliaceae
description: The hollies (Ilex) are evergreen or deciduous trees and shrubs with small greenish-white flowers on separate male and female plants.

name: Araliaceae
description: Ivies, fatsias, umbrella trees (Schefflera) and ginseng are mostly woody, tropical plants with large leaves and flowers in umbels.

name: Araucariaceae
description: Norfolk Island pine, bunya pine, kauri and the Wollemi pine are very tall conifers with tiered branches and large cones.

name: Aspleniaceae
description: A worldwide family of ferns with creeping or upright rhizomes and undivided or divided fronds, growing on the ground or on other plants.

name: Basellaceae
description: Malabar spinach and ulluco belong to a small family of climbing or trailing herbaceous vines, some grown for their leaves or tubers.

name: Campanulaceae
description: Bellflowers, lobelias, balloon flowers and the native isotomas: mostly perennial herbs, often with milky sap and blue star- or bell-shaped flowers.

name: Capparaceae
description: The caper family, about 430 species in the order Brassicales, best known for the caper bush (Capparis).

name: Caprifoliaceae
description: Honeysuckles, abelias and weigelas are hardy shrubs and vines with tubular, often fragrant flowers. Japanese honeysuckle is invasive outside its native range.

name: Colchicaceae
description: Autumn crocus (Colchicum) and gloriosa lily are herbaceous perennials from corms or rhizomes that contain colchicine.

name: Cunoniaceae
description: The family includes the leatherwoods (Eucryphia). Most are evergreen trees and shrubs with opposite or whorled leaves, and Australia and Tasmania have more of its genera than anywhere else.

name: Cupressaceae
description: Junipers, cypresses, arborvitae, redwoods and the native cypress-pines (Callitris): mostly evergreen conifers with scale-like leaves.

name: Cyatheaceae
description: The scaly tree ferns are tall tree ferns with large divided fronds, found in moist forests.

name: Dennstaedtiaceae
description: Bracken and the ground ferns Hypolepis and Dennstaedtia are large, finely divided ferns that spread by rhizomes.

name: Dicksoniaceae
description: Tree ferns (Dicksonia) and Calochlaena are mostly terrestrial or short-trunked ferns with large pinnate fronds.

name: Droseraceae
description: Sundews, the Venus flytrap and the waterwheel plant are carnivorous plants that trap insects and grow in nutrient-poor, boggy soil.

name: Dryopteridaceae
description: The wood ferns and shield ferns are a large worldwide family of mostly terrestrial ferns, many grown in gardens.

name: Eupomatiaceae
description: Eupomatia has three evergreen shrubs and small trees with fragrant flowers, from rainforests and humid forests of eastern Australia and New Guinea.

name: Heliotropiaceae
description: A family of about 450 species of herbs, shrubs, lianas and small trees, mostly from the tropics and subtropics.

name: Linaceae
description: A worldwide family of about 250 species of herbs, subshrubs, vines and small trees.

name: Loranthaceae
description: The mistletoes and the Western Australian Christmas tree, woody plants that mostly grow as partial parasites on host trees.

name: Meliaceae
description: The mahogany family, including toon (Toona ciliata) and white cedar (Melia azedarach): mostly evergreen trees and shrubs with pinnate leaves.

name: Nephrolepidaceae
description: Nephrolepis, including the Boston ferns, which have long, narrow fronds and are popular as pot plants.

name: Nothofagaceae
description: The southern beeches (Nothofagus), including N. cunninghamii, N. moorei and N. gunnii: trees and shrubs that often dominate temperate forests.

name: Osmundaceae
description: Royal ferns and Todea are large ancient ferns, some with trunks up to about a metre, whose spore-bearing fronds look like flowers.

name: Pandanaceae
description: Pandanus and its relatives are trees, shrubs and climbers with long, narrow leaves arranged in a spiral.

name: Philydraceae
description: Helmholtzia, Philydrella and Philydrum make up a small family of tropical perennials from Southeast Asia and Australia.

name: Phyllanthaceae
description: The leaf-flower family (Phyllanthus and relatives) is mostly woody tropical plants and herbs without latex.

name: Phytolaccaceae
description: The pokeweeds (Phytolacca) are a small family in the order Caryophyllales.

name: Picrodendraceae
description: A small subtropical to tropical family of trees and shrubs found in Australia, New Guinea and New Caledonia, close to the leaf-flower family.

name: Piperaceae
description: Peppers and peperomias are herbs and small woody plants with fragrant leaves, growing on the ground or on other plants.

name: Podocarpaceae
description: The podocarps are mostly southern conifers, with their greatest variety in Australasia.

name: Polygalaceae
description: The milkworts (Polygala) are herbs, shrubs and small trees with small, irregular flowers.

name: Polygonaceae
description: Docks (Rumex), buckwheats (Eriogonum) and Muehlenbeckia are mostly perennial herbs with swollen stem joints, along with some shrubs and vines.

name: Polypodiaceae
description: Staghorns (Platycerium) and the family's other ferns nearly all grow on trees or rocks in wet climates.

name: Primulaceae
description: Primroses and cyclamen are mostly perennial herbs, and many of them are garden favourites.

name: Psilotaceae
description: The whisk ferns (Psilotum and Tmesipteris) are primitive plants with no true roots or leaves, anchored by underground stems.

name: Pteridaceae
description: Maidenhair ferns (Adiantum) and brakes (Pteris) are terrestrial or rock-dwelling ferns with compound fronds and rhizomes.

name: Putranjivaceae
description: Drypetes and Putranjiva are evergreen tropical trees with leathery leaves that taste peppery when fresh.

name: Ranunculaceae
description: Buttercups, clematis, delphiniums, hellebores and aconites are mostly herbaceous plants, and many are poisonous or irritate the skin.

name: Restionaceae
description: The restiads are tufted or spreading rush-like herbs with green jointed stems, with about 150 species in Australia.

name: Rhamnaceae
description: The buckthorns, including the native Pomaderris and Cryptandra: mostly trees, shrubs and some vines, most common in warmer regions.

name: Santalaceae
description: Sandalwoods (Santalum) and Exocarpos are partial parasites that draw water and nutrients from host plants.

name: Smilacaceae
description: The greenbriers (Smilax) are woody-rooted climbers, some thorny and some herbaceous.

name: Stylidiaceae
description: Grass-like herbs and small shrubs found mainly in Australia and New Zealand.

name: Thymelaeaceae
description: Daphnes and the Australian Pimelea are mostly shrubs and trees with fibrous bark, and many are poisonous if eaten.

name: Viburnaceae
description: The viburnums and the elders (Sambucus) are shrubs and small trees with toothed opposite leaves and clusters of small flowers.
